resources.string: Lets Focus Tracker detect what kind of content is playing in YouTube so it can categorize your usage. Outside YouTube it only notices which app is in front; screen content is read only inside YouTube.

"Convert my plan below into ONE JSON file for my task app. Output only the JSON inside a single code block, with no commentary.

Format:
{
 "schema_version": 1,
 "tasks": [
 {
 "title": "required, short, max 200 characters",
 "date": "YYYY-MM-DD, the day I should do it",
 "deadline": "YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm (24-hour)",
 "priority": "high | medium | low",
 "estimated_minutes": 45,
 "tags": ["short", "labels"],
 "notes": "optional extra details",
 "subtasks": [
 { "title": "required", "completed": false, "deadline": "optional" }
 ]
 }
 ]
}

Rules:
- Only "title" is required. Leave out any field you are not sure about instead of guessing.
- Today's date is {TODAY}. Never use dates before today.
- Subtasks are one level only (no subtasks inside subtasks).
- Spread tasks sensibly across days. Do not put more than about 6 tasks on one day.
- Use plain text only. No markdown inside values.

My plan:
[PASTE YOUR PLAN HERE]"
